subject: Private deployment DPA: escrow / BYOK / operator access (MedSentry)
messages:
From: Pete Hall <pete.hall@medsentry.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@medsentry.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines + BYOK / operator questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the performance profile. Our legal/security folks pushed back on a few DPA items and asked us to share an initial redline. See attached (MedSentry-DPA-Redlines_v3.pdf). Two headline asks: 1) they want an escrow option for customer keys if Redwood is ever acquired or insolvent, and 2) strict operator access limits for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) — they want operator breakglass to be limited and logged, with quarterly attestation.

Can you confirm whether you support an escrow arrangement (preferred: third-party escrow with split HSM deposit) and what operator telemetry / audit data you can provide? Also we need a list of subprocessors you rely on for Private deployments and any cross-border transfer assurances for EU data.

Happy to schedule a quick call; copying legal.

Thanks,
Pete
Pete Hall
Director, Infrastructure Security
MedSentry

Subject: Re: DPA redlines + BYOK / operator questions

Pete — thanks for the redlines, and great to hear the demo resonated. Quick answers up front:

- Escrow: we can support a third-party escrow approach (we've used KeyShield and Cryptostore in the past). We prefer an HSM-backed split-key escrow (customer retains one shard, escrow agent another) to avoid full custody transfer.
- Operator access: we limit operator access by role, require breakglass approval by two SRE leads, and emit detailed audit logs sent to customer (syslog/S3) for all privileged actions. We can provide quarterly attestation reports.
- Subprocessors / transfers: we'll provide a current subprocessors list and a data flow map for the private deployment pattern you plan to use. For EU residency we have region-pin options and can commit to routing EU data to EU-hosted compute for the deployment.

That said, your redlines request a very broad escrow right (section 7.b) and a prescriptive breakglass timeframe that will be operationally risky. I'd like to propose a middle path: conditional escrow (triggered only on insolvency or change of control + court order) + defined emergency access workflow with post-incident attestation and customer-held audit stream.

Looping in Laura for legal redline coordination and Karthik/Olga for technical specifics. If that works, I'll draft a short amendment that maps to your PDF.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Security & GTM
Redwood Inference

Marissa — quick tech notes to support the amendment draft:

- Escrow mechanics: we recommend a 2-of-3 split where MedSentry holds one key share, the escrow agent holds one, and Redwood the third (or two-of-three with HSM attestations). This avoids Redwood being able to unilaterally reconstruct customer keys.
- Breakglass: define & limit the "emergency window" in the DPA (e.g., 48 hours for initial access, 7 days max retention of snapshot) but require customer notification and signed attestation. All breakglass actions must produce immutable audit events (timestamped, hashed) that are exported to the customer's audit endpoint.
- Telemetry: we can export operator activity as JSONL to a customer S3 endpoint or push via syslog; we include the actor, action, target, keystore-id, and full syscall-level trace for forensic purposes.

I'll attach a short sketch of clause language in the next message (attached keystore-operator-surface.txt) that maps to your PDF sections 7–9.

-Karthik
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA redlines + BYOK / operator questions

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick responses and for looping in your security/legal team. We reviewed Karthik's notes and a few follow-ups from our side:

1) Escrow: we prefer to avoid a full escrow unless absolutely necessary. Our counterproposal: Redwood must support HSM-wrapped BYOK where the customer controls the master key in their HSM (split-key acceptable) and Redwood may only keep an encrypted escrow envelope that is unreadable without the customer's share plus escrow agent approval. If Redwood insists on retaining any reconstructible share, that's a non-starter.

2) Subprocessors: please provide a definitive list and contractually commit to notify us 30 days before adding any subprocessor that will have network-level access to customer metadata.

3) Cross-border: MedSentry requires a hard commitment that production inputs tagged as EU-origin will not leave EU-bound compute unless we provide explicit consent. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support an EU-only private deployment (customer VPC + EU-region nodes) and sign an addendum on data routing?

4) Auditability: our compliance team requires quarterly attestation plus one annual on-site SOC sampling (can be remote for now) covering private deployment operator actions.

If you can accept the above, we can move to a rapid redline pass. Otherwise we'll need to escalate to procurement/legal for further negotiation.

Regards,
Sarah Lee
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
MedSentry

Sarah / Pete — thanks, this is helpful. Summary and my proposed next steps below so we can converge quickly: 

Summary of alignment:
- Escrow / BYOK: Redwood agrees to an HSM-first BYOK model. We will not retain any single reconstructible key share. Our proposed escrow pattern: encrypted escrow envelope that requires (a) customer share + (b) escrow agent approval OR (c) court order with mutually agreed process. We will not hold a unilateral reconstructible secret.
- Subprocessors: we'll deliver a current subprocessors list by EOD Wednesday and contractually promise 30-day notice for any new subprocessors with network access.
- EU routing: we can support EU-only private deployments (EU VPC + EU nodes) and will sign a routing addendum.
- Auditability: Redwood will provide automated operator-audit exports (JSONL to customer S3) and quarterly attestations. We are open to a remote SOC sampling exercise annually.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood legal (Laura) will circulate a short amendment that: replaces section 7.b with the HSM/escrow pattern above, adds 30-day subprocessor notice language, and includes routing addendum stub.
2) Technical appendix from Karthik/Olga to describe telemetry payload and retention (attached: keystore-operator-surface.txt).
3) I'll attach the amendment draft to a DocuSign envelope for MedSentry review; link below.

If that sounds right I'll share the draft by COB today. Thanks for moving quickly on this — we know these clauses can be a blocker so want to make it painless.

Best,
Marissa
Head of Customer Security & GTM, Redwood Inference
